front.title: Speculative Decoding Coordination Protocol (SDCP) for Distributed Inference with Multi-Level Caches

abstract.t: Speculative decoding accelerates language model inference: a small draft model proposes several tokens and the large target model verifies them in one forward pass. In large deployments, draft models and the target model run on separate, independently scaled instances that exchange state through a multi-level cache. This document specifies the Speculative Decoding Coordination Protocol (SDCP), with which a router assigns requests to draft instances by load, draft instances submit proposals that reference draft state in the cache, and a verifier, the only party that commits output, checks proposals under a registered acceptance rule, returns the accepted tokens and the next-round speculation limit, and escalates persistently rejected sessions to a reduced speculation length, another draft model, or decoding by the target model itself depending on its load. SDCP defines a session contract, a committed-prefix digest chain, CBOR messages carried over HTTP, idempotent rounds, and epoch fencing for recovery.
